# Module `tasks`

tasks - spawn self-contained unit-of-work and await its result.

Unlike the threads module, a task is "fire-and-forget": task_spawn starts the
closure on a detached pthread and immediately returns a task handle. The task
delivers its result to a private capacity-1 channel (the handle *is* that
channel), so the caller decides when to wait:

  task_await(t)  blocks until the value arrives and returns it.
  task_poll(t)   returns the value if it is ready, else -1 (non-blocking).
  task_free(t)   reclaims the task handle; returns 0 or -1.

Because the worker is detached there is no join/RAII obligation — simply await
or poll once the result is needed, then free the handle. Note that task_poll
returns -1 both while a task is still running *and* as a legitimate result
value of -1, and that after a successful task_await the private channel is
empty, so a subsequent task_poll reports -1 (the value was already dequeued).

Usage:
  import tasks
  t = task_spawn(|| -> 40 + 2)
  v = task_await(t)    // 42
  task_free(t)         // 0

  t2 = task_spawn(|| -> 99)
  while (task_poll(t2) == -1) { }   // spin until ready (see header caveat)
  v2 = task_poll(t2)
  task_free(t2)
